findings.title: First CCC committer can permanently capture a weekly round by withholding reveal
findings.description: commit_round is permissionless and initializes the one PDA for a week. The payer may supply a fresh Switchboard randomness account under its own authority. After that account wins the unique PDA race, no cancel, expiry, replacement, or recovery instruction exists. Refusing to reveal leaves the round permanently unsettled.
preconditions: Attacker can fund one Solana transaction and a Switchboard randomness account
Attacker submits the first valid commit for the current CCC week
impact: All CCC-linked positions requiring that week are unable to settle it
Affected positions cannot satisfy the all-52-weeks close condition
Residual reward reservations remain locked indefinitely
A low-cost external actor can repeatedly deny CCC liveness
remediation: Restrict commit authority or make commit participation slashable
Add a bounded expiry and permissionless recovery/recommit path that cannot enable selective rerolls
Define deterministic failure settlement for expired rounds
Prove the recovery state machine with local-validator/SBF and signed Devnet adversarial tests
closureEvidence: Regression showing a malicious first committer cannot block the week
Recovery does not permit outcome shopping or candidate-set changes
Independent review of final randomness state machine

findings.title: One address combines program upgrade, administrator, and 500M-IAT custody authority
findings.description: The same public address is hard-coded as PROGRAM_ADMIN and COMMUNITY_CUSTODY and is planned as the upgrade authority. An upgrade authority can replace program logic governing PDA vaults. The combined key therefore correlates direct community custody, eligibility/agency administration, and arbitrary future program behavior.
preconditions: Loss, coercion, compromise, or malicious use of the single hardware-backed authority
impact: Community allocation loss
Malicious program upgrade can authorize transfers from program-owned vaults
Eligibility and agency registry manipulation
No independent control remains to contain the compromise
remediation: Separate community custody, program administration, and upgrade authority
Put high-value authorities behind independent multi-party approval
Choose and publish a timelocked multisig or make the reviewed program immutable after final verification
Test compromise, signer-loss, and emergency migration procedures
closureEvidence: Independent bytecode/source verification after final authority state

findings.title: Pending node UUID acts as a bearer credential across wallet, country, and X binding
findings.description: The wallet proof endpoint returns nodeId, but later country selection and X authorization require only that UUID. There is no bound server session or fresh wallet proof. The callback then places nodeId in a rewards URL. Possession of a leaked pending UUID is sufficient to select the immutable country and attach the possessor's X account to another wallet's pending record.
preconditions: Attacker obtains a pending UUID from browser history, logs, analytics, referrer leakage, shared device state, or another disclosure
impact: Joint control of wallet and X is not established
Victim binding can be poisoned or denied
Genesis ordering and CCC identity records can be corrupted
remediation: Issue an HttpOnly Secure SameSite session bound to wallet, challenge, origin, and pending node
Require fresh wallet authorization for immutable country and X-link transitions
Never place authorization-capable node identifiers in URLs
Consume one-time transition nonces atomically

findings.title: X Premium is an owner-required identity control but is not requested, stored, or enforced
findings.description: The accepted participant unit permits multiple accounts but requires X Premium for every unique wallet/X pair. The callback requests /2/users/me without user.fields=subscription_type and stores only the immutable X user ID. A non-Premium account therefore activates identically to a Premium account.
preconditions: Attacker controls any ordinary X account and a unique wallet
impact: The intended per-identity cost is bypassed
Unlimited non-Premium account farms can compete for Genesis and daily rewards
Audit records cannot prove eligibility at activation or epoch time
remediation: Request subscription_type for the authenticated user
Define the exact allowed Premium tiers and fail closed on None, missing, or unknown values
Persist the observed tier and observation time without persisting OAuth tokens
Define revalidation, downgrade, appeal, and X API outage behavior
closureEvidence: Public policy digest including allowed tiers

findings.title: Documented atomic first-1,000 Genesis reservation is absent from the live schema and routes
findings.description: The blueprint defines genesis_slots with a 1..1000 primary key and an atomic activation/reservation transaction. The applied Drizzle migrations have only a nullable unique genesis_slot column. The OAuth callback marks a binding active but never allocates a slot, checks the cap, or performs the documented transaction.
preconditions: Reward binding service is enabled in its current form
impact: First-come ordering is undefined
Concurrent activations do not enforce exactly 1,000 slots
Active records can be created without the required Genesis capacity decision
Public claim totals cannot be reconciled to the documented ledger
remediation: Make the production schema match the reviewed ledger contract
Allocate from pre-created 1..1000 slots and activate in one serializable D1 transaction
Return CAPACITY_REACHED without losing the verified binding
Test 999/1000/1001 and concurrent final-slot races

findings.title: Release and bundled-framework dependency trees contain critical/high advisories
findings.description: At review time, root npm audit reports 1 critical and 12 high advisories, primarily through electron-builder and tar; the site npm tree reports 7 high and 15 moderate advisories, including Solana bigint-buffer and bundled framework/build paths. Production-only npm sets report zero, but release tools and generated/bundled artifacts remain in scope. The stale pnpm lock reports an additional divergent vulnerable graph.
preconditions: A vulnerable code path processes attacker-controlled build/archive/RPC/image/server-action input or a compromised dependency/build source
impact: Build-runner file overwrite or denial of service
Framework SSRF/DoS or image-processing exposure depending on bundled reachability
Solana integer buffer corruption in affected calls
Release provenance ambiguity
remediation: Upgrade electron-builder and vulnerable transitive tar chain
Upgrade or override bigint-buffer and affected web/framework packages
Regenerate one canonical lock per workspace
Run npm audit and cargo audit as required CI gates
Document reachability for any temporary exception
closureEvidence: Clean high/critical audit result for the canonical release locks
Rebuilt artifacts and full regression suite
Documented exception with reachability proof if a vendor patch is unavailable

findings.title: CCC candidate registry can be padded with unbonded, inactive, or unverified agency wallets
findings.description: The administrator may register any unchecked public owner. Registration requires no owner signature, Premium-bound node proof, stake, active position, bond, or expiry. Selection snapshots every registered agency, so padding the denominator reduces the probability that an economically active agency is paused. One-wallet uniqueness does not stop multi-wallet padding, which is acceptable only when every wallet/X pair satisfies the intended Premium cost and registration policy.
preconditions: Administrator error, collusion, compromise, or an off-chain registration policy that accepts unqualified wallets
impact: Pause probability can be diluted
Capitalized operators can buy denominator share
Inactive candidates can absorb weekly selections
Published draw remains mathematically uniform but economically non-representative
remediation: Define the eligible candidate set economically, not just append-only
Require owner consent and a Premium-verified node attestation
Require an active position, bounded bond, or epoch-specific eligibility snapshot
Specify removal/expiry without enabling operator rerolls

findings.title: Permitted multi-account daily rewards have no published aggregate budget or participant ceiling
findings.description: The policy intentionally pays each qualifying wallet/X pair and permits one 12-IAT claim per pair per day. It specifies a small capped distributor operational wallet but no exact epoch cap, lifetime promotion budget, refill rule, or maximum number of daily participants. Premium cost is external and changeable, so rational account creation expands whenever expected rewards exceed subscription and operating cost.
preconditions: Multiple Premium pairs are economically profitable to operate
impact: Unbounded aggregate daily liability relative to an unspecified distributor cap
First-mover and high-capital concentration
Reward interruption or discretionary refill pressure
Market and community expectations diverge from actual finite funding
remediation: Publish exact per-epoch and lifetime budgets in base units
Define deterministic pro-rata or cutoff behavior when demand exceeds budget
Cap hot-wallet refill and require independent approval
Model break-even account-farm economics across Premium price and IAT price ranges

findings.title: No independent final-code security audit, fuzz campaign, or adversarial SBF integration report exists
findings.description: Repository tests and the signed Devnet rehearsal establish useful functional evidence, but the repository's own policy requires independent security testing proportional to value at risk. This package is an internal Codex-assisted review, not independent assurance. Existing docs explicitly stated that no security or economic review had occurred.
preconditions: Mainnet launch proceeds using only internal evidence
impact: Latent account-constraint, CPI, oracle, economic, or release flaws may remain
Material policy requirement is unmet
Final deployed bytecode is not independently tied to a security opinion
remediation: Fix critical/high findings first
Commission an independent Solana/Anchor audit of the final commit
Add property/fuzz tests and local-validator adversarial flows
Bind the report to source, SBF hash, program ID, and final authority model

findings.title: Production vesting clock starts at config initialization rather than successful activation
findings.description: Production initialize_config records the current clock as genesis. Activation can occur later after multiple funding and authority stages. A failed or delayed ceremony therefore advances vesting and CCC clocks while the program is inactive; the timestamp cannot be reset on the same config PDA.
preconditions: Initialization succeeds but later ceremony stages are delayed or fail
impact: Public Genesis time can diverge from contract Genesis
Vesting and CCC availability can advance during HOLD
Recovery may require abandoning the initialized deployment
remediation: Bind Genesis timestamp to a reviewed activation rule or enforce a maximum initialization-to-activation window
Specify irreversible partial-ceremony recovery
Test delayed activation boundaries

findings.title: Public network lookup can amplify requests into expensive RPC scans without an abuse budget
findings.description: One unauthenticated query may issue multiple upstream calls and a getProgramAccounts scan. The handler uses timeouts and validates inputs but has no endpoint-level rate limit, cache, concurrency budget, or cost accounting.
preconditions: Attacker can send repeated valid address lookups
impact: RPC quota/cost exhaustion
Explorer latency or outage
Pressure on fallback endpoints
remediation: Add per-client and global budgets
Cache immutable/finalized responses
Bound getProgramAccounts frequency and response size
Return generic upstream failures

findings.title: X OAuth outbound calls lack explicit timeouts and redirect configuration is not allowlisted
findings.description: Token and profile fetches have no AbortSignal deadline. X_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI is trusted from configuration without an exact production allowlist. These are operational and configuration trust gaps rather than current secret exposure.
preconditions: X API stalls or deployment configuration is wrong/compromised
impact: Worker resource exhaustion
OAuth outages
Authorization codes or flows directed to an unintended callback
remediation: Use bounded AbortSignal timeouts
Allowlist exact HTTPS callbacks
Apply no-store/referrer controls and structured redacted errors

findings.title: Epoch engine accepts regex-shaped wallets and hashes non-canonical policy JSON
findings.description: Wallet validation checks only Base58 character/length shape and does not decode exactly 32 bytes. policyHash uses ordinary JSON.stringify, so semantically equal objects with different key insertion order have different digests. The launch evidence system already has an RFC 8785 canonicalizer but this engine does not use it.
preconditions: Malformed eligible-row or differently ordered policy input reaches manifest generation
impact: Unclaimable or unintended wallet leaf
Cross-implementation policy digest disagreement
Epoch hold after publication
remediation: Decode and require an exact 32-byte Solana public key
Use the repository RFC 8785 canonical JSON implementation
Domain-separate leaf and internal-node encodings with binary lengths

findings.title: npm and pnpm locks describe divergent site dependency graphs
findings.description: CI uses package-lock.json and npm ci, while a stale pnpm-lock.yaml remains tracked with older Next, React server DOM, Vite, Undici, WS, and Sharp versions. Tools or operators choosing pnpm reproduce a different, more vulnerable graph.
preconditions: Developer, scanner, or release process uses the non-canonical lock
impact: Non-reproducible builds
Conflicting advisory results
Accidental regression to older vulnerable packages
remediation: Remove the unused lock or regenerate and continuously assert equivalence
Declare npm/package-lock as the only canonical site package manager

findings.title: Electron permission handlers auto-approve media/display capture without navigation containment
findings.description: The desktop overlay correctly enables sandbox and context isolation, but its global permission handlers automatically approve media/display-capture requests. No will-navigate or setWindowOpenHandler restriction is installed. A future renderer navigation or content-injection bug could expand into screen/microphone capture.
impact: Local privacy exposure
remediation: Authorize only the expected local file origin and initiating frame
Block remote navigation and new windows
Require explicit user gesture and visible capture state

findings.title: Strict Rust clippy gate is not clean
findings.description: cargo fmt and all Rust tests pass, but clippy with -D warnings fails on framework-generated divergence warnings and local source-organization/argument-count warnings. This is not an exploit, but it weakens a useful zero-warning review gate.
impact: New warnings can be hidden in existing noise
CI lacks a strict Rust lint signal
remediation: Move local items before the test module
Refactor or narrowly allow reviewed argument-count cases
Narrowly allow only verified framework-macro warnings and add clippy to CI
